mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes scalar and vector quantities?

options.A: A scalar has magnitude only, whereas a vector has both magnitude and direction.
options.B: A scalar has direction only, whereas a vector has magnitude only.
options.C: Both scalar and vector quantities have magnitude and direction.
options.D: Neither scalar nor vector quantities have magnitude.

mcqs.answer: A scalar has magnitude only, whereas a vector has both magnitude and direction.
mcqs.explanation: Scalars are described by a single number (magnitude) such as mass or temperature. Vectors need two pieces of information: magnitude and a specific direction, e.g., displacement or velocity. Hence option A is correct; the other options misstate the definitions.

mcqs.question: A displacement of 5 m towards the north is to be drawn as a vector. Which of the following sketches correctly represents this vector?

options.A: A 5 cm arrow drawn upward (pointing north).
options.B: A 5 cm arrow drawn to the right (pointing east).
options.C: A 5 cm arrow drawn downward (pointing south).
options.D: A 5 cm arrow drawn to the left (pointing west).

mcqs.answer: A 5 cm arrow drawn upward (pointing north).
mcqs.explanation: In a standard diagram, north is represented by an upward direction. Therefore the upward arrow correctly shows a vector of 5 m north. The other arrows point in different directions and do not match the required displacement.

mcqs.question: A car moves with a speed of 60 km/h towards the east. Which statement correctly describes its velocity?

options.A: Its velocity has a magnitude of 60 km/h and a direction of east.
options.B: Its velocity has a magnitude of 60 km/h but no specified direction.
options.C: Its velocity has an unspecified magnitude but a direction of east.
options.D: Its velocity has a magnitude of 60 km/h and a direction of north.

mcqs.answer: Its velocity has a magnitude of 60 km/h and a direction of east.
mcqs.explanation: Velocity is a vector quantity; it requires both magnitude (speed) and direction. Here the magnitude is 60 km/h and the direction is east, making option A correct. Options B and C omit one of the required components, and D gives the wrong direction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following physical quantities is a vector?
mcqs.explanation: Displacement specifies both how far an object has moved (magnitude) and the direction of that movement, making it a vector. Mass, temperature, and energy are scalar quantities because they are described solely by magnitude.

mcqs.question: The distance traveled by a runner is a vector because it has a magnitude. Is this statement correct?

options.B: False, because distance has no direction.
options.C: False, because distance becomes a vector only when a direction is specified.
options.D: True, because all physical quantities are vectors.

mcqs.answer: False, because distance has no direction.
mcqs.explanation: Distance is a scalar; it measures the total length of the path irrespective of direction. Only displacement, which includes direction, is a vector. Therefore option B correctly identifies the misconception.

mcqs.question: Two vectors of equal magnitude are drawn tail‑to‑tail, one pointing east and the other pointing north. What is the angle between the two vectors?
mcqs.explanation: East and north are perpendicular directions on a standard Cartesian plane, forming a right angle of 90°. Hence the angle between the vectors is 90°. The other angles correspond to parallel or opposite directions, which do not apply here.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares speed and velocity?

options.A: Both speed and velocity have magnitude and direction.
options.B: Speed has magnitude only, whereas velocity has both magnitude and direction.
options.C: Speed has direction only, whereas velocity has magnitude only.
options.D: Both speed and velocity are scalar quantities.

mcqs.answer: Speed has magnitude only, whereas velocity has both magnitude and direction.
mcqs.explanation: Speed is a scalar—it tells how fast an object moves, without direction. Velocity is a vector—it includes both the magnitude (speed) and the direction of motion. Therefore option B accurately captures the distinction; the other options mischaracterize one or both quantities.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets contains only vector quantities?
mcqs.explanation: Velocity, acceleration, and momentum each require both magnitude and direction, making them vectors. In option A, work is a scalar; option C lists only scalars; option D also consists of scalars. Hence option B is the only set of pure vectors, a typical JEE‑style question.
